# AI Path Finder

> Free AI career consultation (AI role consultation / AI career counselling). A questionnaire matches software engineers, testers, DevOps and data engineers, freshers, MCA/BCA graduates and career changers from non-IT fields to the best-fit AI role. It explains why the role fits and gives a personalised, dated learning roadmap.

Last updated: 2026-10-28

## How the recommendation works
- About 20 questions in 5 sections: background and experience, skill levels (Python, SQL, cloud, AI/ML, maths), a 4-question reasoning check, working style and interests, goals and weekly study hours.
- Self-ratings are checked against the reasoning questions, and contradictory answers are corrected.
- Each of the 9 roles is scored with weighted, explainable signals. Users see a fit %, readiness %, skill gaps, transferable strengths and a roadmap that skips what they already know.
- Everything runs in the browser. Answers are not sent to a server.

## AI career paths
- [AI Foundations Path](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/ai-foundations-beginner.html): Build the base, then land a junior AI / ML role. Best for: students, graduates and people new to coding. Time to job-ready: 4.8 months at 10 h/week. Coding: basic Python; maths: basic statistics.
- [ML Engineer](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/ml-engineer.html): Build, train and ship ML models into real products. Best for: backend and data developers who enjoy data and maths. Time to job-ready: 3.9–5.3 months at 10 h/week. Coding: comfortable Python; maths: basic statistics.
- [Data Engineer (AI focus)](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/ai-data-engineer.html): Build the data pipelines every AI system depends on. Best for: data engineers, BI analysts and SQL-heavy developers. Time to job-ready: 3–3.5 months at 10 h/week. Coding: comfortable Python; maths: very little.
- [AI Product Engineer](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/ai-product-engineer.html): Ship AI features users love — chat, search, copilots. Best for: frontend, full-stack and mobile developers. Time to job-ready: 3–3.2 months at 10 h/week. Coding: basic Python; maths: very little.
- [MLOps / AI Platform Engineer](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/mlops-engineer.html): Run AI reliably and cheaply at scale. Best for: DevOps, cloud, SRE and infrastructure engineers. Time to job-ready: 2.5–3.5 months at 10 h/week. Coding: comfortable Python; maths: very little.
- [LLM / Agent Engineer](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/llm-agent-engineer.html): Build AI agents that plan, use tools and get work done. Best for: backend developers and automation / QA engineers. Time to job-ready: 2.5–3.2 months at 10 h/week. Coding: comfortable Python; maths: very little.
- [AI Research Engineer](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/ai-research-engineer.html): Train, fine-tune and push the limits of models. Best for: people with strong maths who love deep technical work. Time to job-ready: 3.2–5.3 months at 10 h/week. Coding: advanced Python; maths: strong (linear algebra, calculus, probability).
- [AI Forward Deployed Engineer](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/ai-forward-deployed-engineer.html): Deploy AI inside real businesses, hands-on with customers. Best for: senior engineers who enjoy clients and know an industry. Time to job-ready: 2.3–3.5 months at 10 h/week. Coding: comfortable Python; maths: very little.
- [AI Product Manager](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/roles/ai-product-manager.html): Decide what AI should build — and make it succeed. Best for: PMs, BAs, team leads and non-IT domain experts. Time to job-ready: 3–3.2 months at 10 h/week. Coding: not required (low-code is fine); maths: basic statistics.

## AI career guidance by background
- [Software testers and QA engineers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/software-testers-qa.html): usually fits LLM / Agent Engineer, then AI Product Engineer or ML Engineer.
- [Java, .NET and backend developers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/java-dotnet-backend-developers.html): usually fits LLM / Agent Engineer, then AI Product Engineer or ML Engineer.
- [Frontend and full-stack developers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/frontend-full-stack-developers.html): usually fits AI Product Engineer, then AI Forward Deployed Engineer or AI Product Manager.
- [DevOps, cloud and SRE engineers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/devops-cloud-engineers.html): usually fits MLOps / AI Platform Engineer, then AI Forward Deployed Engineer or ML Engineer.
- [Data engineers and BI analysts](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/data-engineers-analysts.html): usually fits Data Engineer (AI focus), then ML Engineer or AI Forward Deployed Engineer.
- [Freshers, students and MCA / BCA graduates](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/freshers-mca-bca-graduates.html): usually fits AI Foundations Path, then ML Engineer or AI Research Engineer.
- [Non-IT professionals (finance, healthcare, teaching, operations)](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/non-it-professionals.html): usually fits AI Product Manager, then AI Forward Deployed Engineer or AI Foundations Path.
- [Product managers, project managers and business analysts](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/product-managers-business-analysts.html): usually fits AI Product Manager, then AI Forward Deployed Engineer or AI Foundations Path.
- [Senior engineers, architects and tech leads (10+ years)](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/for/senior-engineers-tech-leads.html): usually fits AI Forward Deployed Engineer, then AI Product Manager or AI Product Engineer.

## Guides
- [How to choose the right AI role: a 5-step framework](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/guide/how-to-choose-an-ai-role.html): Pick the AI role that reuses most of what you already do, matches the kind of work you enjoy every day, and fits your honest comfort with coding and maths and the hours you can study. Then test it with one small project before you commit months to it. For most working professionals that means an adjacent move rather than starting over: backend to LLM / Agent Engineer, frontend to AI Product Engineer, DevOps to MLOps, data to AI Data Engineer, and PMs or domain experts to AI Product Manager.
- [How the AI career consultation works](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/guide/how-it-works.html): the questions, validation rules, scoring signals per role, and limitations.

## Learn: free AI courses (English and Hinglish)
- [Learn hub](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn.html): 9 courses, one per AI role, following each roadmap step by step. 54 lessons, each with a real-life analogy, a plain-language explanation, key terms, a worked example and a quick check. Every lesson is available in English and Hinglish (Hindi in Roman script with English technical terms).
- [What is AI? AI vs ML vs Deep Learning vs GenAI](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/what-is-ai.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/what-is-ai.html): AI ⊃ Machine Learning ⊃ Deep Learning ⊃ Generative AI. Each is a more specific part of the one before.
- [Python basics: variables and data types](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/py-basics.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/py-basics.html): A variable is a labelled box, and every value inside it has a type.
- [Python logic: if/else, loops and functions](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/py-logic.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/py-logic.html): if = decide, loop = repeat, function = reuse.
- [Lists and dictionaries: storing many values](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/py-collections.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/py-collections.html): List = ordered line of items. Dictionary = look up by name (key).
- [Git and GitHub: saving and sharing your work](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/git-github.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/git-github.html): add → commit → push. Commit small and often, with clear messages.
- [Pandas: working with tables of data](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/pandas.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/pandas.html): DataFrame = table. Most AI projects start with load → clean → groupby.
- [Averages and spread: mean, median, variance](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/stats-center-spread.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/stats-center-spread.html): Use the median when there are outliers, and always look at the spread too.
- [Probability and distributions](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/stats-probability.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/stats-probability.html): Model outputs are usually probabilities, and you pick the threshold.
- [Correlation vs causation, and sampling bias](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/stats-correlation.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/stats-correlation.html): Correlation is not causation, and biased data gives biased AI.
- [SQL basics: asking a database questions](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/sql-basics.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/sql-basics.html): SELECT what → FROM where → WHERE which rows → GROUP BY → ORDER BY.
- [SQL JOINs: combining tables](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/sql-joins.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/sql-joins.html): INNER = only matches. LEFT = keep everything on the left.
- [How machines learn: features, labels and training](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ml-how-machines-learn.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ml-how-machines-learn.html): Features in → label out. Training = learning from examples with known answers.
- [Two kinds of prediction: regression and classification](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ml-regression-classification.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ml-regression-classification.html): Number → regression. Category → classification. Start simple.
- [Train/test split and overfitting](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ml-train-test.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ml-train-test.html): Never judge a model on data it trained on.
- [Measuring models: accuracy, precision and recall](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ml-metrics.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ml-metrics.html): Beat the baseline, and choose precision vs recall by the cost of each mistake.
- [What is an LLM? Tokens, context and temperature](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/llm-what.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/llm-what.html): LLM = super-powered next-word predictor. Mind tokens, context and temperature.
- [Prompting: giving clear instructions to an LLM](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/llm-prompting.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/llm-prompting.html): Role + context + task + format + examples. Then test and iterate.
- [Calling an LLM API: keys, requests and costs](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/llm-api.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/llm-api.html): Request in → response out, billed per token. Guard the key, and handle errors.
- [Building a portfolio project that gets interviews](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/portfolio.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/portfolio.html): Real problem, end-to-end, evaluated, deployed and well explained.
- [Landing the AI role: resume, applications and interviews](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/job-search.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/job-search.html): Action + result + number. Reframe your experience in AI terms. Apply steadily.
- [Feature engineering: turning raw data into useful inputs](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ml-features.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ml-features.html): Good features + domain knowledge > fancy algorithms. Watch out for leakage.
- [Decision trees, random forests and boosting](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ml-trees.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ml-trees.html): Tables → try boosted trees first.
- [Vectors and matrices: the language of AI](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/math-vectors.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/math-vectors.html): Everything in AI becomes vectors, and similarity is just vector maths.
- [Gradients and gradient descent: how models improve](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/math-gradients.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/math-gradients.html): Gradient = which way is downhill. Learning = many small steps down the loss hill.
- [Neural networks: layers that learn](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/dl-neural-networks.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/dl-neural-networks.html): Layers of weighted sums plus activations, trained by backprop.
- [Transformers and attention: how LLMs read](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/dl-transformers.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/dl-transformers.html): Tokens → vectors → many attention layers → next-token prediction.
- [Training vs inference: how ML runs in production](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ml-training-vs-inference.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ml-training-vs-inference.html): Training creates the model. Inference serves it, fast, cheaply and reliably.
- [Serving a model as an API with FastAPI](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/api-serving.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/api-serving.html): Model → API endpoint → any app can use it. Validate inputs and log everything.
- [Docker: packaging your app so it runs anywhere](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/docker.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/docker.html): Dockerfile (recipe) → image (package) → container (running app).
- [MLOps: experiment tracking and model registries](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/mlops-tracking.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/mlops-tracking.html): Log every run, register every shipped model, and always be able to roll back.
- [Monitoring models: drift and silent failures](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/mlops-monitoring.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/mlops-monitoring.html): Models decay silently. Monitor inputs, outputs and outcomes, with alerts.
- [Data modelling: designing tables for analysis](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/data-modeling.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/data-modeling.html): Facts = what happened (numbers). Dimensions = descriptions.
- [Data pipelines: ETL, Airflow, dbt and Spark](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/data-pipelines.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/data-pipelines.html): Extract → transform → load, orchestrated, tested, re-runnable and monitored.
- [Data quality: catching bad data early](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/data-quality.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/data-quality.html): Check completeness, validity, uniqueness, consistency and freshness, automatically.
- [Embeddings and vector databases: searching by meaning](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/embeddings.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/embeddings.html): Embeddings = meaning as numbers. A vector DB finds the nearest meanings fast.
- [RAG: letting an LLM answer from your documents](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/rag.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/rag.html): RAG = search your docs, then answer from them with citations.
- [Streaming data: Kafka and real-time pipelines](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/streaming.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/streaming.html): Batch = periodic, simpler. Streaming = real-time, more complex. Use it when seconds matter.
- [Evaluating AI: how to know it actually works](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/llm-evals.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/llm-evals.html): No evals, no confidence. Measure every change.
- [AI safety in products: hallucinations, prompt injection and guardrails](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/llm-safety.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/llm-safety.html): Treat model output and documents as untrusted. Limit what tools can do.
- [UX for AI features: designing for uncertainty](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ai-ux.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ai-ux.html): Stream it, source it, let users edit it, and learn from feedback.
- [Tool use (function calling): letting an LLM take actions](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/llm-tool-use.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/llm-tool-use.html): The model asks, your code acts. Validate everything.
- [Serving LLMs efficiently: GPUs, batching and cost](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/gpu-serving.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/gpu-serving.html): Batch requests, measure latency and cost, and quantise and cache where you can.
- [Kubernetes: running containers at scale](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/kubernetes.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/kubernetes.html): Declare the desired state, and Kubernetes keeps it true: restarts, scaling, updates.
- [AI agents: plan, act, observe, repeat](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/llm-agents.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/llm-agents.html): Agent = LLM + tools + loop + memory + guardrails.
- [MCP: a universal plug for AI tools](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/llm-mcp.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/llm-mcp.html): MCP = one standard plug between AI apps and your tools and data.
- [Fine-tuning and LoRA: specialising a model](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/dl-fine-tuning.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/dl-fine-tuning.html): Prompting → RAG → fine-tuning, in that order of cost.
- [Reading and reproducing research papers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/research-papers.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/research-papers.html): Skim first, then go deep, then reproduce. Reproduction is proof.
- [Enterprise AI: integration, security and compliance](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/security-compliance.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/security-compliance.html): Enforce access, mask PII, log everything, and involve security early.
- [Problem framing: should AI solve this, and how?](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/problem-framing.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/problem-framing.html): Problem → metric → data → simplest solution. Diagnose before you prescribe.
- [Explaining AI to non-technical people](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/stakeholder-communication.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/stakeholder-communication.html): Outcome → evidence → risk → ask. Analogies over jargon. Demos over slides.
- [AI literacy for decisions: build vs buy, cost and limits](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/build-vs-buy.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/build-vs-buy.html): Buy → API → RAG → fine-tune → build. Climb only when needed.
- [Prototyping AI ideas with low-code tools](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/no-code-prototyping.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/no-code-prototyping.html): Prototype in days, test with real users, then write the spec.
- [Metrics and A/B testing for AI features](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ab-testing.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ab-testing.html): Define success and guardrails first, then randomise and wait for significance.
- [Writing an AI product spec (PRD) with an eval plan](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/ai-prd.html) · [Hinglish](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/learn/hi/ai-prd.html): Problem, metric, scope, UX for failure, eval plan, risks, launch bar.

## Interview practice
- [Interview practice with scoring](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview.html): role-specific questions (multiple-choice scored automatically, open questions self-checked against model answers). The report gives a score per skill area, explains each mistake and links the lessons for every gap.
- [AI Foundations Path interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/ai-foundations-beginner.html): 38 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 21 quiz questions. Typical rounds: HR or recruiter screen (15 to 30 min); Online test; Technical interview; Managerial or HR round.
- [ML Engineer interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/ml-engineer.html): 53 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 27 quiz questions. Typical rounds: Recruiter screen; Coding round; ML fundamentals; ML system design; Behavioural and project deep dive.
- [Data Engineer (AI focus) interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/ai-data-engineer.html): 42 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 26 quiz questions. Typical rounds: Recruiter screen; SQL round; Python or Spark round; Pipeline and data modelling design; Behavioural.
- [AI Product Engineer interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/ai-product-engineer.html): 43 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 24 quiz questions. Typical rounds: Recruiter screen; Coding round; AI feature design; System design; Craft deep dive on an AI feature you built, plus behavioural.
- [MLOps / AI Platform Engineer interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/mlops-engineer.html): 35 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 16 quiz questions. Typical rounds: Recruiter screen; Coding or scripting round; MLOps concepts; System design; Incident and behavioural round.
- [LLM / Agent Engineer interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/llm-agent-engineer.html): 44 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 22 quiz questions. Typical rounds: Recruiter screen; Coding round; RAG and evals deep dive; System design; Project deep dive and behavioural.
- [AI Research Engineer interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/ai-research-engineer.html): 34 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 18 quiz questions. Typical rounds: Recruiter screen; ML coding; Math and fundamentals; Research discussion; Behavioural and team fit.
- [AI Forward Deployed Engineer interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/ai-forward-deployed-engineer.html): 37 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 23 quiz questions. Typical rounds: Recruiter screen; Coding round; Decomposition case (the hardest round); Technical depth; Customer and behavioural round.
- [AI Product Manager interview questions and answers](https://homesh123.github.io/ai-career-advisor/interview/ai-product-manager.html): 39 commonly asked questions in interview order (introduction, fundamentals, role skills, design, behaviour, salary) with easy model answers, plus 24 quiz questions. Typical rounds: Recruiter screen; Product sense; Analytical and metrics; AI depth; Behavioural and leadership.

## Quick answers
- Which AI role should a software engineer choose? It depends on current work. Backend developers often fit LLM / Agent Engineer, frontend and full-stack developers fit AI Product Engineer, DevOps engineers fit MLOps / AI Platform Engineer, data engineers fit Data Engineer (AI), and senior client-facing engineers fit AI Forward Deployed Engineer.
- Is there an AI role for people who don't code? Yes. AI Product Manager suits PMs, business analysts and domain experts such as accountants, teachers and healthcare professionals.
- Can freshers or MCA graduates get into AI? Yes. Start with the AI Foundations path (Python, statistics, SQL, ML basics, two portfolio projects), or go straight to ML Engineer if you already have strong ML projects.
- How long does it take? Usually 3 to 9 months at around 10 hours a week, depending on starting skills and the target role.
